b.5d9cd092c0:
<h>Invitatorium</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Regem Evangelistárum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem Evangelistárum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>V</c>eníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem Evangelistárum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem Evangelistárum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>H</c>ódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem Evangelistárum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem Evangelistárum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
b.a798b75820:
<h>Invitatory</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Regem Evangelistárum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem Evangelistárum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>C</c>ome let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem Evangelistárum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>F</c>or the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>F</c>or the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. <n>(genuflect)</n> Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem Evangelistárum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>T</c>oday if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>F</c>orty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem Evangelistárum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.

<r>Cap. 7</r>
<c>L</c>ucas médicus Antiochénsis ut eius scripta índicant, Græci sermónis non ignárus, fuit discipulus ac sectátor Apóstoli Pauli, et omnis peregrinatiónis eius comes. Scripsit Evangélium, de quo idem Paulus: Mísimus, inquit, cum illo fratrem, cuius laus est in Evangélio per omnes ecclésias. Nam de ipso Paulum intellexisse plerique sanctorum Patrum affírmant. In Acháie Bœotiǽque pártibus Evangélium conscripsísse sanctus Hierónymus refert.

<h>Reading 4</h>
Ex S. Hieron. de Script. eccl. et ex aliis antiquis Patribus
<r>Cap. 7</r>
<c>L</c>uke was a physician of Antioch, who, as appeareth from his writings, knew the Greek language. He was a follower of the Apostle Paul, and his fellow traveller in all his wanderings. He wrote a Gospel, whereof the same Paul saith We have sent with him the brother, whose praise is in the Gospel throughout all the Churches <n>2 Cor. viii, 18</n> Of him, he writeth unto the Colossians, <n>iv, 14</n>: Luke, the beloved physician, greeteth you. And again, unto Timothy, <n>2 Cor. iv, 11</n>: Only Luke is with me. He also published another excellent book entitled The Acts of the Apostles, wherein the history is brought down to Paul's two years sojourn at Rome, that is to say, until the fourth year of Nero, from which we gather that it was at Rome that the said book was composed. Nam de ipso Paulum intellexisse plerique sanctorum Patrum affírmant. In Acháie Bœotiǽque pártibus Evangélium conscripsísse sanctus Hierónymus refert.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

<r>℟.</r> These men are holy, for they are the friends of God.

b.de44fcec8d:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>O</c>ctober 19th 2027, the 19th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Rome, under the Emperor Mark Antonine, the holy martyrs Ptolemy and Lucius. Of these it is recorded by Justin Martyr that Ptolemy brought a lewd woman to believe in Christ, and taught her to honour chastity, for the which cause he was accused by an unclean man before Urbicius the Prefect. He suffered a long and foul imprisonment, and at length made a public confession of Christ's teaching, and was sentenced to death. Lucius blamed the sentence and openly avowed himself also to be a Christian, for the which cause he was sent to death likewise, and with them was sent a third under the same condemnation.
<h>A</h>t Antioch, the holy martyrs Beronicus, the Virgin Pelagia, and forty-nine others.
<h>I</h>n Egypt, in the persecution under the Emperor Maximin, the holy soldier Varus. He used to visit seven holy monks that were kept in prison, and to minister to them, and when one of them died he chose to be substituted in his place, and along with the others he suffered great cruelties, and gained the palm of martyrdom.
<h>A</h>t Evreux, (at the end of the seventh century,) the holy Confessor Aquilinus, Bishop (of that see.)
<h>I</h>n the country of Orleans, (toward the end of the sixth century,) deceased holy Veran, Bishop (of Cavaillon.)
<h>A</h>t Salerno, (in the fifth century,) holy Eusterius, Bishop (of that see.)
<h>I</h>n Ireland, (at the end of the sixth century,) the holy Confessor Ethbin.
<h>A</h>t Oxford, in England, (in the eighth century,) the holy Virgin Frideswide, (Patroness of that city. She was daughter of the Prince of that territory, and founded at Oxford a nunnery in honour of St. Mary and all the saints, the direction of which was committed to her care.)
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

b.bfdf302cc2:
<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>Sir 15:1-2</r>
<c>Q</c>ui timet Deum, fáciet bona: et qui cóntinens est iustítiæ, apprehéndet illam, et obviábit illi quasi mater honorificáta.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>E</c>xsúltet cælum láudibus,
Resúltet terra gáudiis:
Apostolórum glóriam
Sacra canunt solémnia.

<h>V</h>os sæcli iusti iúdices,
Et vera mundi lúmina,
Votis precámur córdium,
Audíte preces súpplicum.

<h>Q</h>ui cælum verbo cláuditis,
Serásque eius sólvitis:
Nos a peccátis ómnibus
Sólvite iussu, quǽsumus.

<h>Q</h>uorum præcépto súbditur,
Salus, et languor ómnium:
Sanáte ægros móribus,
Nos reddéntes virtútibus.

<h>U</h>t, cum Iudex advénerit
Christus in fine sǽculi,
Nos sempitérni gáudii
Fáciat esse cómpotes.

<h>D</h>eo Patri sit glória,
Eiúsque soli Fílio,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
Et nunc, et in perpétuum.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum.
<r>℟.</r> Et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.
b.d13845c3eb:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Sir 15:1-2</r>
<c>Q</c>ui timet Deum, fáciet bona: et qui cóntinens est justítiæ, apprehéndet illam, et obviábit illi quasi mater honorificáta.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>N</c>ow let the earth with joy resound,
And heaven the chant re-echo round;
Nor heaven nor earth too high can raise
The great Apostles' glorious praise.

<h>O</h> ye who, throned in glory dread,
Shall judge the living and the dead,
Lights of the world forevermore!
To you the suppliant prayer we pour.

<h>Y</h>e close the sacred gates on high;
At your command apart they fly:
Oh! loose for us the guilty chain
We strive to break, and strive in vain.

<h>S</h>ickness and health your voice obey;
At your command they go or stay:
From sin's disease our souls restore;
In good confirm us more and more.

<h>S</h>o when the world is at its end,
And Christ to judgement shall descend,
May we be called those joys to see
Prepared from all eternity.

<h>P</h>raise to the Father, with the Son,
And Holy Spirit, Three in One;
As ever was in ages past,
And so shall be while ages last.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth:
<r>℟.</r> And their words unto the ends of the world.
